title: Other Node core modules
lede: The smaller Node built-ins, grouped here rather than each given a full page. net, tls, http and https are Node's own layering ported to TypeScript — a net.Socket is a Duplex over a native TCP handle, a TLSSocket a Socket whose handle carries a non-blocking OpenSSL session, and http/https build on them — all on one event loop with dgram and dns. Messages across process and channel boundaries (cluster, diagnostics_channel) are strings, and vm stays out of scope behind the same blocker as bare eval().

entries.name: querystring (.parse, .stringify, .escape, .unescape)
entries.signature: querystring.parse(str: string, sep?: string, eq?: string, options?: ParseOptions): ParsedUrlQuery; querystring.stringify(obj?: ParsedUrlQueryInput, sep?: string, eq?: string, options?: StringifyOptions): string
entries.description: Node's legacy "a=b&c=d" parse/stringify, ported from Node's own lib/querystring.js. parse returns a null-prototype object; a repeated key collects its values into an array; a leading '?' is plain text (unlike new URLSearchParams(str)). stringify takes an object whose array values repeat the key. Custom separators, maxKeys and custom encode/decode functions are honoured; escape, unescape, unescapeBuffer, encode and decode are exported too.

params.name: str / obj
params.desc: A raw query tail to parse, or an object to serialize.

params.name: sep, eq
params.desc: The pair and key/value separators ('&' and '=' by default).

returns.desc: The parsed object, or the serialized query string.

entries.name: assert (.ok, bare assert(cond, msg?), .equal/.strictEqual, .notEqual/.notStrictEqual, .deepEqual/.deepStrictEqual (+not*), .fail, .throws, .match/.doesNotMatch)
entries.signature: assert(value: unknown, message?: string | Error): asserts value; assert.strictEqual(a, b); assert.deepStrictEqual(a, b); assert.throws(fn, error?); await assert.rejects(promise)
entries.description: Node's assertion library, ported from Node's own sources: the same checks, the same AssertionError (name, code, actual, expected, operator), and the same failure messages and diffs, including assert.ok quoting the failing call's source. Distinct from console.assert, which logs and continues.
differences: No `assert.CallTracker` (deprecated in Node)
Deep equality does not compare symbol-keyed properties, and a failure diff does not invoke getters
An uncaught `AssertionError` prints `Uncaught: <message>` rather than Node's name, stack and property block

entries.name: test / node:test
entries.signature: import test, { describe, it } from 'node:test'; test(name, options?, fn); import { mustCall } from 'test'
entries.description: Node's test runner: tests run after the module, one at a time in registration order, with describe/it suites, skip/todo, the TestContext (t.test, t.skip, t.todo, t.diagnostic, t.plan) and before/after/beforeEach/afterEach hooks, reported in Node's spec format with its summary and a nonzero exit on failure. The bare 'test' specifier is Node's own test-suite helpers: mustCall/mustCallAtLeast (counts checked at exit), mustSucceed, mustNotCall, expectsError, expectWarning, skip, and the platform probes.

returns.desc: Registration, or a counting wrapper of the callback.

differences: A failing test's details omit Node's `test at <file>:<line>:<col>` line and the stack: the error prints as `Name [code]: message`.
No `mock.*`, `run()`, snapshots, concurrency, timeouts, `t.signal`/`t.assert`, or `only` filtering.
The spec reporter prints without colors on a terminal (Node colors it); no other reporter.

entries.name: util (.inspect, .format)
entries.signature: util.format(fmt?: any, ...args): string; util.inspect(value, options?): string; util.isDeepStrictEqual(a, b): boolean; util.promisify(fn); util.callbackify(fn)
entries.description: Node's util, ported from Node's own lib/util.js: format and formatWithOptions walk the specifiers at run time as Node does (%s calls a program's own toString), inspect takes depth, compact, sorted, breakLength and maxArrayLength, and callbackify, deprecate, debuglog, styleText, types and the system-error lookups behave as Node's.

params.name: fmt
params.desc: A format string for .format (any string, at run time).

differences: `.promisify` wraps a function value and honours `promisify.custom`; a code-generated builtin (`fs.readFile`) is not a function value to pass it
`promisify(f) === f` is false for an already-promisified `f`
`.inspect` ignores `colors`, `showHidden`, `getters`, `maxStringLength`, `numericSeparator` and `[inspect.custom]` methods; `compact: true` is treated as 3
No `inherits`, `parseArgs`, `MIMEType` or `getCallSites`

entries.name: net (TCP server: net.createServer, server.listen/address()/on('connection'|'listening')/close; TCP client: net.connect/createConnection (positional or { port, host }); connection socket .on('data'|'end')/.write/.end/.address()/.destroy()/.setNoDelay()/.setKeepAlive(); net.isIP/isIPv4/isIPv6)
entries.statusRow: net (TCP server: net.createServer, server.listen/address()/on('connection'|'listening')/close; TCP client: net.connect/createConnection (positional or { port, host }); connection socket .on('data'|'end')/.write/.end/.address()/.destroy()/.setNoDelay()/.setKeepAlive(); net.isIP/isIPv4/isIPv6)
entries.description: Node's lib/net.js ported to TypeScript over native TCP handles on the event loop. A Socket is a Duplex — back-pressure and 'drain', pause/resume, setEncoding, setTimeout, ref/unref; Server listens by port/host/backlog/options or a Unix-socket path, dual-stack :: by default. Errors are built as Node builds them (connect ECONNREFUSED, getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, with .code/.errno/.syscall/.address/.port).
differences: `connect`/`createConnection` take a port, an options object or `{ path }`; the connect is non-blocking and a failure arrives as an async `'error'` then `'close'`
`listen`'s `'listening'` and `'error'` fire on the next tick, as in Node; `maxConnections` and `getConnections` are supported; `isIP`/`isIPv4`/`isIPv6`
BlockList, SocketAddress and happy-eyeballs address selection (`autoSelectFamily`) are not ported
On Windows the TCP handles are compile-checked, not yet run

entries.name: dgram (UDP sockets: createSocket('udp4'), bind, address(), setBroadcast(), on('message'), send, close)
entries.statusRow: dgram (UDP sockets: createSocket('udp4'), bind, address(), setBroadcast(), on('message'), send, close)
entries.signature: dgram.createSocket('udp4' | 'udp6' | options, listener?); socket.bind(port?, address?, cb?); socket.send(msg, port, address, cb?)
entries.description: Node's UDP sockets: udp4/udp6, bind with 'listening', send in every form (offset/length, lists, before the bind completes), connect/disconnect, the broadcast/TTL/multicast options and group membership, buffer sizes, ref/unref. 'message' receives a Buffer and { address, family, port, size }.
differences: Sends are synchronous, so getSendQueueSize()/getSendQueueCount() are always 0.
The lookup and block-list options, bind({ fd }) and cluster-shared sockets are not ported.
Windows: TTL/multicast options and membership apply to udp4 sockets only (compile-checked, not run).

entries.name: tls (TLS-wrapped sockets)
entries.signature: tls.connect(port, host[, {rejectUnauthorized}][, onSecureConnect]); tls.createServer({ cert, key }, connectionListener)
entries.description: Node's _tls_wrap shape in TypeScript: a TLSSocket is a net.Socket whose handle carries a non-blocking OpenSSL session, so the handshake runs on the event loop. tls.connect supports servername, rejectUnauthorized, ca/cert/key and ALPN, firing 'secureConnect' with authorized/authorizationError and Node's verify error codes and messages; tls.createServer emits 'secureConnection' and 'tlsClientError'; createSecureContext, getProtocol and getCipher.
differences: OpenSSL-only (libssl) — a `-crypto=commoncrypto` build using `tls` is a clean compile error (Mac's CommonCrypto has no TLS API)
Session resumption, OCSP, renegotiation, PSK and `getPeerCertificate()`'s certificate object are not ported
On Windows the TCP handles are compile-checked, not yet run

entries.name: dns (dns.lookup, dns.resolve4/resolve, dns.promises.lookup)
entries.signature: dns.lookup(host, [options,] cb); dns.resolve4(host, [{ ttl }], cb); dns.resolveMx(host, cb); new dns.Resolver(options); await dns.promises.lookup(host)
entries.description: Node's own lib/dns.js. lookup and lookupService run getaddrinfo/getnameinfo on the thread pool, as libuv does (all, family, hints, order); the resolve family — resolve4/6 with TTLs, MX, TXT, SRV, NS, CNAME, PTR, SOA, NAPTR, CAA, TLSA, ANY, reverse — is a native DNS client in c-ares' place: the system's servers, UDP with TCP on truncation, Resolver timeouts, tries, setServers, cancel and setLocalAddress, and Node's error codes (ENOTFOUND, ENODATA, ETIMEOUT, …). dns.promises and dns/promises are the promise forms.

returns.desc: The request (callbacks arrive on a later tick), or a Promise.

differences: A resolve error has no `errno` key (Node's has `errno: undefined`)
The Windows server discovery and DNS client are compile-checked only

entries.name: zlib (gzip/gunzip, deflate/inflate, deflateRaw/inflateRaw, unzip, each *Sync + (err, result) callback)
entries.statusRow: zlib (gzip/gunzip, deflate/inflate, deflateRaw/inflateRaw, unzip, each *Sync + (err, result) callback)
entries.signature: zlib.gzipSync(input, options?): Buffer; zlib.gzip(input, options?, (err, out) => …); zlib.createGzip(options?): Gzip; zlib.crc32(data, value?): number
entries.description: Node's zlib module: the Deflate/Inflate/Gzip/Gunzip/DeflateRaw/InflateRaw/Unzip streams and their create* functions, the one-shot methods (callback and *Sync), crc32, constants and codes, with every zlib option. Each stream owns a native zlib handle whose writes run on the thread pool. Input may be a Buffer/TypedArray, ArrayBuffer, DataView, or string (UTF-8); output is always a Buffer.

params.name: input
params.desc: The data to compress or decompress.

params.name: options
params.desc: flush, finishFlush, chunkSize, windowBits, level, memLevel, strategy, dictionary, info, maxOutputLength, rejectGarbageAfterEnd.

returns.desc: The compressed/decompressed bytes (a stream for create*).

differences: Brotli and Zstd load the system libbrotli/libzstd at run time (Node bundles them); where they are missing, a Brotli or Zstd stream is `ERR_ZLIB_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`
Compressed bytes are the system libz's, which can differ from Node's bundled zlib at the same level (each inflates the other's)
A `*Sync` call with `info: true` is typed `{ buffer, engine }` (@types types it `Buffer`)

entries.name: vm (vm.Script, sandboxed eval-like execution)
entries.description: Not implemented. vm hits the same fundamental blocker as bare eval() — there is no embedded engine to run source assembled at runtime. An opt-in embedded-engine path is scoped but not started.

entries.name: diagnostics_channel (channel/subscribe/unsubscribe/hasSubscribers/tracingChannel, Channel, TracingChannel)
entries.description: Node's module: named channels whose subscribers receive any published value and the channel name; bound stores and runStores; tracing channels that publish start/end/asyncStart/asyncEnd/error around traceSync, tracePromise and traceCallback. A subscriber's throw is reported on the next tick without stopping the others.

returns.desc: A channel, a tracing channel, a subscription result, or nothing.

entries.name: http client (http.get/http.request)
entries.signature: http.get(url, res => …); const req = http.request(opts); req.write(body); req.end()
entries.description: Node's _http_agent/_http_client in TypeScript over net. http.get and http.request return a ClientRequest (an OutgoingMessage) and the response is an IncomingMessage — a Readable.

returns.desc: A request handle; the response arrives via callback.

differences: ClientRequest: chunked or `Content-Length` bodies, `'response'`/`'socket'`/`'information'`/`'upgrade'`/`'error'`, `abort`/`destroy`/`setTimeout`
`http.Agent` pools keep-alive sockets; `http.globalAgent` keeps them alive and unref'd, as Node 19+
`http.request(new URL(…))` is not accepted — pass a string or an options object

entries.name: https (client: https.get/https.request)
entries.signature: https.get(url, res => …); const req = https.request(opts); req.end()
entries.description: https.createServer is a tls.Server running the http module's connection handling; https.request/get/Agent/globalAgent connect with tls.connect. Same request and response objects as http.

returns.desc: A request handle; the response arrives via callback.

differences: Same client limit as `http` for a `URL` argument

entries.name: stream/web (re-exports: ReadableStream/WritableStream/TransformStream/CompressionStream/DecompressionStream)
entries.description: The names bind as identity to the ambient WHATWG constructors that already exist — importing them from stream/web is interchangeable with using the globals. The queuing-strategy classes are not exported.

returns.desc: The same ambient constructors as the globals.

entries.name: cluster (fork, worker messaging, isPrimary/isWorker/worker, Worker.id/.process)
entries.signature: cluster.fork(env?); cluster.on('listening', (worker, address) => {}); cluster.workers[id]; cluster.setupPrimary(settings); cluster.disconnect(cb?)
entries.description: Node's cluster module. The primary forks workers that run this same program; a worker's net or http server listens through the primary, which either accepts connections and hands them to the workers in turn (round-robin, the default outside Windows) or gives every worker the listening socket itself. Workers and the primary exchange messages, handles included, over the fork channel.
differences: `setupPrimary({ exec })` naming another file fails at `fork()`: a worker is this compiled program, so there is no other script for it to run
`inspectPort` and the inspector flags are ignored: a compiled program has no inspector
A `dgram` socket bound in a worker binds on its own, not through the primary
Windows: a worker's `listen` does not work yet — descriptor passing over the fork channel is POSIX-only

entries.name: http2 **module** (http2.createServer/connect, Http2Session/Http2Stream)
entries.description: Node's http2 module: HTTP/2 servers (cleartext h2c and TLS with ALPN, optionally answering HTTP/1.1) and client sessions, with the compat request/response API, the core stream API, push streams, settings, ping and goaway.
differences: `respondWithFD`/`respondWithFile` read the whole file into memory before sending it, where Node streams it
`session.altsvc()`/`origin()` validate their arguments but send no frame; `setNextStreamID`/`setLocalWindowSize` validate only
`session.socket` is the raw socket, not Node's Proxy guarding the session-owned socket methods
The `Http2ServerRequest`/`Http2ServerResponse` subclass options are ignored
`stream.write` has no backpressure: it always returns `true` and buffers
Most session tuning options (`maxSessionMemory`, `paddingStrategy`, …) are accepted and ignored

entries.name: async_hooks (AsyncLocalStorage, AsyncResource)
entries.signature: const als = new AsyncLocalStorage<T>(); als.run(store, () => als.getStore()); AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot(); new AsyncResource(type).runInAsyncScope(fn)
entries.description: AsyncLocalStorage carries a store through an async call tree: run/exit/enterWith/getStore/disable and the name/defaultValue options, with the context frame propagating across await (a spawned task inherits it) and into promise reactions and timer, setImmediate, nextTick and queueMicrotask callbacks scheduled inside run(). Static bind/snapshot and AsyncResource (runInAsyncScope, bind) capture the current context and replay it later.
differences: createHook, executionAsyncId, triggerAsyncId and executionAsyncResource are not exported; asyncId() numbers resources in creation order with no lifecycle events behind it.
